newsitem.title: USA: U.S. RFG values speed ahead on tight supply, costs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. RFG values speed ahead on tight supply, costs.

text.p: Reformulated gasoline values in New York Harbor sped ahead Wednesday under upward pressure from tightening supplies and a spiking market for gasoline blendstocks, especially MTBE, players said.
"The reformulated is getting really tight in the Harbor," said one trader.
According to weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) data released late Tuesday, reformulated gasoline (RFG) stocks were down by 1.9 million barrels on the East Coast as of last Friday.
In addition, total imports of RFG showed a hefty 305,000 barrel per day drop to an anemic 52,000 barrels per day.
"The numbers started going up late yesterday after the APIs came out and then we opened up even higher," said a Harbor trader.

In moderate Wednesday activity, differentials on prompt regular northern-grade 87-octane RFG, known to traders as "A2," firmed 1.25 cents over NYMEX August futures, putting sellers at 2.25 cents for delivery by the 25th.
Differentials on prompt "D2," or northern-grade 93-octane premium RFG, rose 1.50 cents to between 10.25 and 10.50 cents over Augu the print.

There appears little relief on the horizon. For the past month, RFG values have been harassed higher by tight supplies and rising prices of MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether), a blending component used either to boost oxygen or octane.
On Wednesday, MTBE was trading around 93.00/94.00 cents a gallon in the U.S. Gulf and 97.00/98.00 cents in the Harbor, a good 6.00 cents above last month.

"A lot of blenders are buying up supply, but it is all hand to mouth. They had held off thinking prices were going to fall but with all the production problems we've been having we've have gone up," said one MTBE trader on the Gulf Coast, the most active spot MTBE market in the U.S.

The latest glitch is ARCO's 20,000 bpd plant in Rotterdam. A company source said the plant, which recently returned online from a turnaround, will shut down for about four to five days for unscheduled maintenance.
The plant exports much of its production to the U.S.
